crossLayerReview: Read the full current defaults-lifecycle.test.ts diff and affected setup/concurrent fixture assertions. The Windows fixture captures a held child creation-time identity before release and compares the same PID/creation-time identity after cleanup; decimal ticks remain text. Only absent PID maps to null, while malformed output, access/query errors and bounded process-launch failures reject. POSIX behavior still uses signal zero and accepts only ESRCH as absent.

The new guard regression rejects a still-live predecessor, then checks its identity after real service.close. Immediate observation of each pending read leaves the original rejecting promise intact; the extra rejecting finally chain becomes two settlement handlers. Existing cache sharing, changed cwd/options/config, generation invalidation, capacity, active/queued close classifications and cleanup-unconfirmed assertions remain.

This Windows test observation change does not alter NativeRpc/service cleanup, the root/native fixed launcher, systemd/cgroup stop proofs, manager forced recovery, journal ownership or unknown receipt preservation. Those exact production bytes retain their existing review and independent regression evidence.

deploy/build.py SOURCE_ROOTS remains src/web/protocol, with the same six top-level source/config manifests. The only changed tests/runtime path is outside the application pack allowlist and all deployment control files are unchanged. No assertion that a newly packed gzip must have identical container bytes, and no permission to deploy the failed CI5 stage is inferred.

The CI5 log lacks original process handles or creation times. PID reuse is a possible explanation, not a proven historical root cause. The author Windows24-case targeted evidence is retained as such; it is not a new full-suite or Linux result.
